title: The concerns over the Census questions
author: K. Narayanan Unni
content_html:
The questions to be asked to every individual during the population enumeration phase of the 2027 Census were notified by the Central government last month. In a significant departure from the past, a number of personal details, which cannot be used to generate any useful statistics, are being sought. This prompts a look at the individual questions, their possible uses and the implications of their inclusion in the Census.

The new questions in Census 2027 ask respondents to provide the details of the parents of every individual and spouses of the married persons in the household, nationality as declared, permanent residential address, place of COVID 19 vaccination, total number of bank accounts, mobile number, Aadhaar number and Voter ID number (if available), Passport number (if an Indian passport holder), and driving license availability.

title: The Lord chooses Tiruvelukkai
content_html:
In Kancheepuram lies the sacred shrine of Tiruvelukkai. The Tamil word ‘Vel’ means desire, and ‘irukkai’ means residing, denoting that Yoga Narasimhar chose to reside here out of His loving desire to bless devotees, said Tirukudanthai Dr. Venkatesh in a discourse. The Sanskrit name of Tiruvelukkai is Kamasika (’Kama’ meaning desire and ‘Asika’ meaning residing); both Tiruvelukkai and Kamasika convey the same meaning. Swami Vedanta Desika composed eight celebrated verses in His praise, titled “Kamasikashtakam”. Quoting the poetic phrase “Ettumaa moorthi......”, Swami Desika highlights the spiritual power of the number eight, signifying that one who sincerely worships the Lord can attain everything worthy of realisation. Across the eight verses, Swami Desika glorifies Lord Narasimha:

First, he honours the miraculous Lion-Man deity who freely chose to dwell along the Vegavathi River, praying for His perpetual presence in his heart. Second, he describes the Lord’s three eyes — representing the Sun, Moon, and Fire — that terrify evil and burn away all physical, mental, and cosmic suffering. Third, the Acharya marvels at how the Lord left Vaikunta to reside on Earth as an accessible form for human worship. Fourth, he proclaims Lord Narasimha as the eternal relative of every soul, resting peacefully in a yogic pose on the riverbank. Fifth, as controller of all senses, the Lord sits in deep yoga, quietly teaching self-control while fulfilling noble desires. Sixth, the Acharya describes the Lord’s mighty arms and sharp nails that defeated Hiranyakasipu, ever ready to defend surrendered souls. Seventh, he highlights the striking contrast between the Lord’s terrifying fury towards the demon king and His soft, motherly tenderness towards Prahlada. Finally, Swami Desika presents the core truth of devotion: if Lord Narasimha protects you, no other protector is needed; if He does not, none can save you. Guided by this trust, the devotee completely surrenders at His feet.

title: Punjab leaders have assured me of working collectively under Rahul and Kharge’s leadership: Sachin Pilot
author: Sandeep Phukan
content_html:
Newly appointed Congress general secretary in charge of Punjab, Sachin Pilot, on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) met Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and party general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra as he took up his new assignment. He faces the challenge of factionalism in the State unit, particularly between former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Pradesh Congress Committee chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring.

title: NIA arrest accused in Saharanpur counterfeit currency case
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested an absconding accused, Amit Kumar, a bank employee and a key accused in the conspiracy relating to counterfeit currency notes at the Punjab National Bank currency chest, Saharanpur, officials said on Tuesday (September 8, 2026).

“The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested an absconding accused, Amit Kumar, a bank employee and a key FIR-named accused in the conspiracy relating to counterfeit currency notes at the Punjab National Bank currency chest, Saharanpur, UP, in case RC-02/2026/NIA/LKW,” reads an official statement.

“On 29th August 2026, PS Sadar Bazar, District Saharanpur, UP, received credible information regarding the recovery of counterfeit Indian currency notes with a face value of ₹17.29 crore from the currency chest of Punjab National Bank, Saharanpur, UP. The involvement of three employees of the bank also surfaced during the inquiry, and they were accordingly suspended by the bank. The case was initially registered as FIR No. 0431/2026, dated 29th August 2026, at PS Sadar Bazar, District Saharanpur, UP, under section 178 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, against 3 accused persons, and was re-registered by NIA on 3rd September 2026. Investigation is ongoing to unfold the complete conspiracy and to arrest the co-accused persons,” the official statement further reads.

title: Keralam planning to take over Elderline operations
author: R K Roshni
content_html:
As uncertainty continues over operations of Elderline, the national helpline for the elderly (toll-free number 14567), in Keralam, the State government plans to take it over and operate it as a round-the-clock helpline.

The government decision to continue the helpline also stems from the plan for starting a Department for the Welfare of the Elderly in the State soon.

Since a 24x7 helpline is on the government agenda as part of its 100-day programme, the government plans to start a State call centre during night-time as the national helpline works only during the day.

Officials say the Union government is planning to wind up Elderline operations. The State has decided to take it over at that stage and transform it into a 24x7 helpline.

Salaries not paid

Meanwhile, though a move to reconfigure the helpline operations, which had caused much concern among the staff, beneficiaries, and the organisations working for elderly welfare, has been put off for the time being, the helpline staff who have been working without pay since the start of this year hope to see funds sanctioned soon.

The staff say there are plans to discontinue the State-level offices and convert the helpline into a centralised zonal project. The operations would be handed over to another agency instead of the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), which is the national implementation agency, and all calls from the elderly in the south zone would connect to a zonal office.

This transition was expected to be effected after the current memorandum of understanding with the State expired on September 30.

However, a communication extending the project in its current form till March 31, 2027, or till further intimation was issued by the Union Ministry recently. The decision has brought some relief to the staff, but for the fact that their salaries since the start of the year and dues to utility providers for electricity, water, and Net connectivity are pending.

The staff say Keralam is awaiting last year’s funds and those till September this year of the 100% Centrally sponsored scheme, even as a majority of the States have been sanctioned funds by the NISD.

Without salary for months, the 10 call officers, three leaders, one project manager, and one finance officer are having a hard time. “What is worse is that funds are being denied for a project run by the government. We are somehow sticking on because of the fact that the State government is involved,” says an employee.

Government officials say they had contacted the Ministry repeatedly and were promised that the funds would be sanctioned soon.
